nodes.title: Send preedit rectangle (not just cursor rectangle) to support stable IME popup positioning
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Hi,

On Wayland, CJK input methods currently only get a cursor rectangle from the app. Because the cursor moves while typing Pinyin, the candidate popup jumps around constantly.

The proposed fix in wayland-protocols is to let apps also send a preedit rectangle, so the input method can anchor the popup to the start of the preedit instead of the moving cursor. See the discussion here:
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/517
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/521

Since Electron apps like VS Code and Slack are very popular on Linux, it would make a huge difference if Electron could send the preedit rectangle via zwp_text_input_v3 (in addition to the cursor rectangle). Without that, input methods can't fix the jumping even if they support the new protocol.

Is there any plan to implement this? I'd be glad to test an early build.

Thanks!


This also affects Chromium upstream. I tried to file an issue at [issues.chromium.org](https://issues.chromium.org/) but couldn't log in. If anyone from the Electron team can help pass this along to the Chromium input team, that would be great.



### Proposed Solution

input methods

### Alternatives Considered

input methods

### Additional Information

_No response_

> This also affects Chromium upstream.

In that case, it should be filed and implemented upstream in Chromium and is not something that Electron should implement downstream. Any chance you can file an upstream issue somehow?

> > This also affects Chromium upstream.
> 
> In that case, it should be filed and implemented upstream in Chromium and is not something that Electron should implement downstream. Any chance you can file an upstream issue somehow?

@nikwen Thanks for the guidance! I was able to file an upstream Chromium issue here:
https://issues.chromium.org/issues/555310815
Please let me know if any additional information is needed from my side.
Closing this out, this fix is dependent on the upstream Chromium bug and we don't track it in two places. Once it's fixed in Chromium it will bubble down into Electron quite quickly

nodes.title: Guidance / workaround request: macOS 15+ CJK font rendering corruption (upstream Chromium hvgl)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker without success

### Problem Description

Electron apps rendering Chinese text on macOS 15+ (Sequoia / Tahoe) can hit CJK glyph corruption when the system font subsystem is in certain states. The root cause is upstream: macOS 15 introduced the private `hvgl` outline format used exclusively by PingFangUI.ttc, and `CGFontCreateWithDataProvider()` returns nil for hvgl bytes. Skia's cross-process typeface reconstruction falls back to family-name lookup, which can pick a different PingFang variant than the one used for shaping, producing a stable per-character CID mismatch (e.g. 工 → ┥, 作 → ﬄ, 辛 → 扳, 苦 → 梧, 了 → Y).

This has been observed across Electron 19 (Chromium 102), Electron 22 (Chromium 108), and Electron 38 (Chromium ~130). Chromium has a partial fix in `printing/common/metafile_utils.cc:490` (see [455517173 comment 4](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173) and fix [8007770](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8007770)) but this only covers the printing path; the on-screen rendering path is still affected on current Chromium.


### Proposed Solution

Any of the following would help downstream apps:

1. **Documentation**: Add a note to Electron macOS docs about the recommended CJK-safe `font-family` stack pattern (put `"PingFang SC"` before `-apple-system` to force run-level match and avoid the Blink char-level fallback path that triggers the mismatch). This is the simplest and confirmed effective workaround.

2. **Cherry-pick evaluation**: Consider evaluating whether the Chromium `metafile_utils.cc:490` fix (or similar rendering-path workaround if/when Chromium lands one) should be backported to Electron LTS branches.

3. **Optional runtime flag**: A CLI flag like `--force-native-cjk-render` that routes CJK glyph rasterization through CoreText's high-level APIs (which handle hvgl natively) instead of the byte-stream serialization path.

Option 1 is the lowest-cost and would help many downstream apps immediately.

### Alternatives Considered

- CSS-only fix in each app: put `PingFang SC` first in the `font-family` stack. Appears to help in the cases we've tested, but we haven't verified this rigorously across every affected Electron/macOS combination. Also requires every affected app to figure this out independently.
- Wait for Apple to publish the hvgl spec: HarfBuzz maintainers have been waiting since 2024; no public timeline that we're aware of.
- Embed a fallback font (e.g. Noto Sans SC) with probe-based auto-heal: adds several MB per app and requires runtime detection logic.

### Additional Information

Related upstream references:
- Chromium: [#380313555](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/380313555), [#455517173](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173)
- HarfBuzz: [#4891](https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/issues/4891)
- FreeType: [#1281](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/freetype/freetype/-/issues/1281)
- fonttools: [#3639](https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools/issues/3639)
- Apple HVF partial docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/hvf

Other apps hitting the same underlying macOS font issue via different code paths: mpv, Servo, Godot, Jellyfin Swiftfin, Parley/Blitz.

Even a short "this is out of scope for Electron, please file with Chromium/Apple" response with any suggested best practice would be genuinely helpful for downstream apps stuck in this workaround limbo.

nodes.title: macOS 15+ CJK garbling in Electron via system PingFang font (upstream Chromium hvgl)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker without success

### Electron Version

22.3.27 (also seen on 19.1.9)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.x and Tahoe 26.4.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not tied to Electron version - triggered by macOS 15+ font subsystem behavior.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Chinese text like "工作辛苦了" renders correctly in Electron app windows.

### Actual Behavior

On some macOS 15+ machines, CJK characters render as unrelated glyphs. Real-world user screenshots show a stable per-character mapping:

```
工 → ┥
作 → ﬄ
辛 → 扳
苦 → 梧
了 → Y
```

The corruption is intermittent - triggered by macOS font subsystem state (both PingFangUI.ttc and AssetsV2 PingFang.ttc present). Restarting the Electron app usually recovers.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Root cause is upstream in Chromium/Skia, not Electron-specific. Chromium already has partial handling in `printing/common/metafile_utils.cc:490` (see [chromium/455517173 comment4](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173) and fix [8007770](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8007770)). The rendering path in main Chromium is still affected.

Filing here for visibility and to check if Electron would consider a backport/workaround for supported branches. If out of scope for Electron, please redirect.

<details><summary>In-depth investigation</summary>

macOS 15 introduced the private `hvgl` outline table used exclusively by PingFangUI.ttc. `CGFontCreateWithDataProvider()` returns nil on the raw hvgl bytes. When Chromium/Skia falls back to `MakeFromName("PingFang SC")` for cross-process rasterization, it can resolve to AssetsV2's PingFang.ttc (CFF format), whose glyph table layout differs entirely from PingFangUI's. The result: text shape produces glyph IDs from PingFangUI's cmap (e.g., 工 → gid 695), which are then rendered against AssetsV2's glyph table (where gid 695 corresponds to ┥).

Minimal API-level reproducer (any macOS 15+):

```swift
import Foundation
import CoreText
let path = "/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/FontServices.framework/Versions/A/Resources/Reserved/PingFangUI.ttc"
let data = NSData(contentsOfFile: path)!
let provider = CGDataProvider(data: data as CFData)!
print(CGFont(provider) as Any)  // nil
print(CTFontManagerCreateFontDescriptorsFromData(data as CFData) as Any)  // 0 descriptors
```

Related upstream references:
- Chromium: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/380313555, https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173
- HarfBuzz: https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/issues/4891
- FreeType: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/freetype/freetype/-/issues/1281
- Fonttools: https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools/issues/3639
- Apple HVF docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/hvf

Other applications hitting the same underlying macOS font issue via different code paths: mpv, Servo, Godot, Jellyfin Swiftfin, Parley/Blitz.

</details>

<!-- end-of-life -->

Hello @oNo500. Thanks for reporting this and helping to make Electron better!

The version of Electron reported in this issue has reached end-of-life and is [no longer supported](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines#timeline). If you're still experiencing this issue on a [supported version](https://releases.electronjs.org/) of Electron, please update this issue to reflect that version of Electron.

Now adding the https://github.com/electron/electron/labels/blocked%2Fneed-info%20%E2%9D%8C label for this reason. This issue will be closed in 10 days if the above is not addressed.
Closing per author's decision - will file with Chromium tracker instead as this is upstream.

41.1.1

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Calling `app.getGPUInfo('complete')` does not cause significant degradation of the  GPU process.

### Actual Behavior

Calling `app.getGPUInfo('complete')` creates a promise which resolves relatively quickly (in around 280ms), however, the GPU process is being blocked for 13 seconds.



### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/59cffe74582e21c16324d7f6c0a79d09

nodes.title: [Bug]: Tray StatusNotifierItem answers property reads on its well-known name but errors on its unique name, breaking GNOME AppIndicator
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu, Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Reproduced on two independent stacks: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS / GNOME 46 / Wayland / kernel 6.8, and Linux Mint 22.3 / Cinnamon / X11 / kernel 6.8.0-136. Tray hosts `gnome-shell-extension-appindicator` and `xapp-sn-watcher` (xapps 3.2.2) respectively.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

28.3.3

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A `Tray`'s StatusNotifierItem should answer `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get` and `GetAll` regardless of whether the request is addressed to its well-known name (`org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1`) or to that name's unique connection name (`:1.NNN`). Per the D-Bus specification a unique name and any well-known name the connection owns are equivalent destinations.

This matters because GDBus clients routinely resolve a well-known name to its unique owner before querying, to avoid races if ownership changes. Both tray hosts tested do exactly that, so the unique-name path is the only one they ever use.

### Actual Behavior

Property reads succeed on the well-known name and fail on the unique name — same process, same object path, same interface, same moment, only the destination differs:

| Call on `/StatusNotifierItem`, iface `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` | via well-known name | via unique name `:1.1219` |
|---|---|---|
| `Properties.GetAll` | OK — 14 properties | **FAIL** |
| `Properties.Get(Status)` | OK | **FAIL** |
| `dbusmenu.GetLayout` | OK | OK |

```
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
```

`:1.1219` is confirmed via `GetNameOwner` to be the owner of that well-known name — it is not a different connection. Note the **menu object answers on both addresses; only the `Properties` interface on `/StatusNotifierItem` discriminates.** The menu is still unreachable in practice, because the host learns the menu's path from the `Menu` property it can never read.

**This is a regression, and the behavioural difference is the well-known name itself:**

| | Electron 28.3.3 (works) | Electron 43.4.0 (broken) |
|---|---|---|
| Well-known name | **none — unique only** | `StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` |
| `GetAll` via unique name | OK — 14 properties | **FAIL** |
| Menu object path | `/com/canonical/dbusmenu` | `/org/chromium/DbusMenu/1` |
| Host outcome | icon + menu | neither |

Electron 28 registered no well-known name at all, so hosts addressed the unique name that already works. Electron 43 registers one and then refuses reads to its own unique owner.

**Control** — a non-Electron indicator on the same session answers the same call shape on its unique name:

```
Get(Id) via :1.115 /org/ayatana/NotificationItem/livepatch -> (<'livepatch'>,)
```

**Host-side confirmation**, `xapp-sn-watcher` with `sn-watcher-debug true`:

```
create_key: Key: 'org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-261894-1/StatusNotifierItem'
sync_skeleton: Syncing icon properties (org.freedesktop.statusnotifieritem-261894-1)
** CRITICAL **: Could not get properties for org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-261894-1:
GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
… no set_icon_from_pixmap, no update_menu — the item is never populated
```

The same watcher on the Electron 28 build, and on other pixmap-only items such as `flameshot` and `copyq`, completes normally.

On GNOME the equivalent failure is raised in `appIndicator.js:_checkNeededProperties` via `statusNotifierWatcher.js:_registerItem`, and in one run the exception left the extension INACTIVE for the rest of the session — removing the tray for **every other app** too.

User-visible outcome: no icon, or a generic missing-image placeholder, and no context menu.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Why "I don't know how to test" for Chrome.** The menu object path moving to `/org/chromium/DbusMenu/1` in the affected version suggests this lives in Chromium's `StatusIconLinuxDbus` backend rather than in Electron's wrapper, and I would expect it to be a Chromium bug. But Chrome does not expose a tray icon in normal desktop use, so I could not construct an equivalent reproduction to confirm it before filing. If a maintainer can confirm the backend, this should be moved to the Chromium tracker — I am happy to refile there.

**Reproduction** with any Electron app that creates a `Tray`, on a session with an SNI host:

1. Find the item's bus name: `gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.DBus --object-path /org/freedesktop/DBus --method org.freedesktop.DBus.ListNames | tr ',' '\n' | grep StatusNotifierItem`
2. Read a property via that well-known name — succeeds:
   ```
   gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 \
     --object-path /StatusNotifierItem \
     --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierItem Id
   ```
3. Resolve the unique owner: `... --method org.freedesktop.DBus.GetNameOwner <well-known-name>`
4. Repeat step 2 against `:1.NNN` — errors.

Steps 2 and 4 are the whole report; the asymmetry between them is the bug.

**Ruled out**, each tested directly against live 28.3.3 and 43.4.0 instances running concurrently on the same machine and session:

- Missing `IconName` / `IconThemePath` — both builds omit them; hosts fall back to `IconPixmap` cleanly, as they do for other apps.
- Empty D-Bus introspection — both builds return `<node></node>`; the hosts do not introspect.
- The icon asset — byte-identical between the two builds, and it renders correctly from the 28.3.3 item.
- A startup race — polling `GetAll` from the instant the bus name appears returns success at t+0ms on the working build, and the failure on 43.4.0 is permanent and reproducible minutes later.
- Wrong interface name — hosts correctly use `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem`.
- Stale registration, desktop shell state, corrupted user config — excluded by restarting app, tray host and shell.

**Workaround, for anyone finding this:** none from application code. There is no command-line switch to suppress the well-known name registration. Not registering one — as Electron 28 did — would sidestep the defect entirely, since clients would then address the unique name that already answers.

Credit: the Cinnamon/X11 measurements, the 28-vs-43 bus-registration comparison and the watcher logs come from a user of my app investigating the regression on his own machine.

<!-- issue-template-check -->

Hello @iamalismith. Thanks for taking the time to open an issue and helping to make Electron better!

This issue was automatically closed because its body does not follow any of this repository's issue templates. Maintainers rely on the sections in those templates to triage issues, and issues that are missing them usually cannot be acted upon.

To get this issue triaged, please either:

* Edit the issue body above to include all of the sections from one of our [issue templates](https://github.com/electron/electron/tree/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE) - it will be reopened automatically once it does, or
* File a new issue via https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/new/choose, which will fill in the correct template for you.

I've bisected this to an exact Electron release, and the result changes the triage: **it is not an Electron 43-vs-28 regression, it landed in Electron 43.3.0** — and **Electron 44 and 45 are still affected**, so upgrading is not a way out.

## Bisect

Verified by running each binary against a StatusNotifierWatcher and reading `Properties.GetAll` on `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` via the well-known name and via that name's unique owner:

| Electron | Chromium | Registration | `GetAll` via unique | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 43.2.0 | 150.0.7871.129 | **no well-known name**; per-icon path `/org/chromium/StatusNotifierItem/1` | **OK** | works |
| 43.3.0 | 150.0.7871.212 | well-known name; shared `/StatusNotifierItem` | **FAIL** | broken |
| 43.4.0 / 43.4.1 | 150.0.7871.224 | as above | **FAIL** | broken |

**Last good: 43.2.0. First bad: 43.3.0.** Both boundary points were confirmed by executing the actual binaries, not only by reading source.

On 43.2.0 the item registers as `:1.NNN@/org/chromium/StatusNotifierItem/1` — unique name plus an explicit object path — and every property reads back normally, with no host-side errors. That is the same shape the report describes for Electron 28, which is why 28 was identified as "last known working": the behaviour actually survived all the way to 43.2.0.

## Source scan across milestones

Presence of `StatusIconLinuxDbus::Multiplexer` / `method_call->GetDestination()` in `chrome/browser/ui/views/status_icons/status_icon_linux_dbus.cc`:

| Chromium | Electron | Multiplexer |
|---|---|---|
| 120, 136, 144, 148 | 28, 36, 40, 42 | absent |
| 150.0.7871.46 (43.0.0) | 43.0.0 | **absent** |
| 150.0.7871.212 (43.3.0) | 43.3.0 | **present** |
| 152.0.7977.30 | 44 | **present** |
| 153.0.8001.0 | 45 | **present** |
| `refs/heads/main` | — | **absent** |

So it was introduced into the 150 branch mid-line (between `.129` and `.212`), is present on the 152 and 153 branches, and has since been removed on `main`. The fix therefore exists upstream but has not reached any shipping branch — which makes this a backport request rather than a design discussion.

## Practical impact

Applications on Electron 43.3.0+ have no supported way out: there is no switch to suppress the well-known name, and moving forward to 44 or 45 does not help. Pinning to **43.2.0** restores the tray, at the cost of the Chromium patches between `150.0.7871.129` and `.224` — a security trade-off that is uncomfortable to recommend, which is really the argument for backporting the `main` state to 43/44/45.

Test harness used, if useful for reproduction: a ~40-line `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` stub (python3-gi) that records registrations, so the test does not depend on a desktop's own tray host. Happy to attach it.

Duplicate of #52674, which predates this by two weeks and is already labelled `blocked/upstream`. My apologies — I searched the tracker before filing and did not find it.

I have folded the evidence from here into that thread: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/52674#issuecomment-5388273064 — specifically the Cinnamon/X11 reproduction (so it is not GNOME- or Wayland-specific), the concurrent 28-vs-43 comparison showing Electron 28 registered no well-known name at all, and the observation that `dbusmenu.GetLayout` answers on BOTH addresses while only `Properties` on `/StatusNotifierItem` discriminates.

Closing in favour of #52674.

Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 25H2 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version N/A ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior N/A ### Actual Behavior when using [Binskim](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/driversecurity/binskim-check-binaries) to check electron binaries using the below command `path\to\BinSkim.exe analyze path\to\electron-v43.4.1-win32-x64\electron.exe --recurse true --output V43.4.1.sarif --local-symbol-directories "path\to\electron-v43.4.1-win32-x64-pdb"` This is part of [CWE-121](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/121.html) its is listing the following vulnerabilities It says that stack protector is disabled in many functions. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Please use this below viewer to view the attached sarif file [V43.4.1.sarif.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31303521/V43.4.1.sarif.zip) https://microsoft.github.io/sarif-web-component/

After reviewing the BinSkim SARIF, I don't believe the BA2014 findings demonstrate that Electron is being built without /GS stack protection.
A few observations:

- The SARIF does not report BA2011 (EnableStackProtection), which is the BinSkim rule used to determine whether stack protection is enabled for a binary overall.
- The BA2014 findings are reported against individual functions rather than the binary as a whole.
- The functions listed in the BA2014 results appear to be almost entirely from upstream Chromium Rust dependencies and generated Rust code, for example: 
- serde_json::*
- read_fonts::*
- skrifa::*
- harfrust::*
- icu_calendar::*
- temporal_rs::*
- crabbyavif::*
- rustfft::*
- other Rust standard library and crate symbols
Given that BA2014 is intended to identify functions compiled with stack protection disabled (historically via constructs such as __declspec(safebuffers)), it is not obvious that these Rust-generated symbols correspond to intentional stack-protection suppression by Electron or Chromium developers.
Combined with the absence of BA2011, this suggests the finding may be the result of how BinSkim interprets metadata emitted by Rust/LLVM-generated code rather than evidence that Electron is broadly compiled without /GS.
I suspect that the results against equivalent Chrome or Edge binaries will have the same Rust-generated symbols triggering BA2014 there as well.
At this point, I do not see evidence that Electron itself is disabling /GS globally, and the findings appear to warrant BinSkim applicability review rather than an Electron code change.

Given Electron's dependency on Chromium, I am going to close this issue as won't fix.

nodes.title: [Bug] `webContents.sendInputEvent` mouse coordinates are mis-scaled by `devicePixelRatio` under fractional-DPR (Linux/Wayland) → clicks land off-target
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 40.10.2 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version CachyOS (Arch-based), kernel 7.1.8-1-cachyos, KDE Plasma on **Wayland** (XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland), NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, 4K display (3840×2160). ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Not known — not tested in an older version. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior A `webContents.sendInputEvent({ type: 'mouseDown'/'mouseUp', x, y, button: 'left' })` mouse click at `(x, y)` should be received by the page at `(x, y)`, so the element at that point is clicked. ### Actual Behavior The click is received by the page at a **mis-scaled position**. On a page where `window.devicePixelRatio` is fractional (here **1.256**), a click sent to `(x, y)` arrives in the page at roughly `(x/DPR, y/DPR)` — about **20% short** of where it was aimed. Any normal-sized link or button at the target point is therefore missed, so programmatic clicking does not navigate. Measured on this machine (sent → received in the page): ``` (50,50) → (39,39) (100,100) → (79,79) (200,150) → (159,119) (400,300) → (318,239) ``` ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/N0tS0Lucky/64a24301d51bc4f735cd9ac85e3d7c1b ### Additional Information
In-depth investigation

**The fractional DPR is triggered by page navigation, not the display config.** On this system the compositor reports `Scale: 1` and there is **no** global or fractional scaling configured (`kwinrc` `Scale=1`, `Xft.dpi=96`, no `GDK_SCALE`/`QT_SCALE_FACTOR`). Yet: - `about:blank` → `window.devicePixelRatio` = **1.0** - `example.com` → `window.devicePixelRatio` = **1.2559** Same window, same display. The DPR jumps to the fractional value only when a real web page is navigated to, pointing at a buffer-scale negotiation on page load (Wayland fractional-scaling path) rather than a user setting. **Isolation already performed:** - Not zoom: reproduced identically at zoom 100% / 90% / 125%. - Not backend: reproduces under default (XWayland), `--ozone-platform=wayland`, and `--ozone-platform=x11` — all report DPR 1.256 on a real page and all mis-place the click identically. - Not window size/visibility: reproduced at 900×600 and 400×300, shown and hidden. - Events still arrive as `trusted: true`; the input is genuine, just mis-positioned. - `pointermove` receives a coordinate that can differ from `mousemove` by one device pixel (e.g. 149,149 vs 148,148), consistent with a DIP↔CSS translation inside the input pipeline. The mis-scale factor exactly tracks `1 / devicePixelRatio`, which points at `sendInputEvent` coordinates being treated in one pixel space while the page reads them in another. Likely the renderer input-translation path is not accounting for the page's fractional `devicePixelRatio`. Minimal repro (also in the gist): ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') app.whenReady().then(async () => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 900, height: 600, show: false }) await win.loadURL('https://example.com/') await win.webContents.executeJavaScript( `window.addEventListener('mousedown', e => window.__m=[e.clientX,e.clientY], true); 'ok'`) win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseMove', x:200, y:150 }) win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseDown', x:200, y:150, button:'left', clickCount:1 }) win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseUp', x:200, y:150, button:'left', clickCount:1 }) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 300)) console.log('DPR', await win.webContents.executeJavaScript('window.devicePixelRatio')) console.log('received at', await win.webContents.executeJavaScript('window.__m')) app.exit(0) }) ```

<!-- issue-template-check -->

Hello @N0tS0Lucky. Thanks for taking the time to open an issue and helping to make Electron better!

This issue was automatically closed because its body does not follow any of this repository's issue templates. Maintainers rely on the sections in those templates to triage issues, and issues that are missing them usually cannot be acted upon.

To get this issue triaged, please either:

* Edit the issue body above to include all of the sections from one of our [issue templates](https://github.com/electron/electron/tree/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE) - it will be reopened automatically once it does, or
* File a new issue via https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/new/choose, which will fill in the correct template for you.

## Windows 11 repro — `webContents.sendInputEvent` mis-scales by guest-page `devicePixelRatio`, with no display scaling in play

Following up on the diagnosis in this issue. I can confirm the core mechanism (`sendInputEvent` coordinates are interpreted as *device pixels* of the renderer buffer, so they land at `sent / DPR`) and can add a Windows 11 datapoint that extends the existing evidence in a way I think matters for the root-cause discussion.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 24H2, build 26100.9445 |
| Display | 2560×1440 single monitor, **100% desktop scaling** (no `LogPixels` value in `HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop`) |
| Electron | 40.10.2 (via the Hermes desktop app, 0.17.2; the page surface is a `<webview>`) |
| Guest content | a MediaWiki login form (a real HTTP page, not `about:blank`) |
| App UI zoom | tested at **150% and 100%** — identical behavior (see below), so app zoom is ruled out |

Two things about this environment are worth calling out up front:

1. **There is no fractional display scaling anywhere** — not in Windows display settings, not in the app's own zoom.
2. So this is a pure "real web page loaded in a webview on Windows at 100% scale" configuration — the cleanest possible Windows test of the navigation-triggered-DPR hypothesis from the `about:blank` vs `example.com` experiments in this thread.

### Repro (concrete, at 100% UI zoom)

The app drives the webview with `sendInputEvent({type: 'mouseDown', x, y})` where `x, y` are computed from the target element's `getBoundingClientRect()` in **CSS pixels**.

Live session on the MediaWiki login form, app UI zoom at **100%**:

1. Username field (`#wpName1`) contains `AuroraBot`. Password field (`#wpPassword1`) is empty, ≈95 CSS px below it.
2. Send `type` action targeting the **password** field (its focus-click + keystrokes).
3. Observed result: the keystroke `X` was received by the **username** field — its value became `XAuroraBot`. The input landed ~95 px *above* the aimed point, i.e. `actual ≈ sent / k` with a fractional `k`, matching the ratio class reported here (not a fixed-pixel offset).
4. Repeat with app UI zoom changed to **150%**: identical behavior. Same at 100%.

Two further observations:

- It is **not specific to one verb**: a bare `click` on the password field mis-targets identically. The mis-scale is in the coordinate mapping, not in the key/insertion path.
- The host app's input funnel applies **no coordinate transformation at all** — the CSS-pixel rect center is sent as-is. (For reference, the same app *does* apply a scale correction in exactly one other path — its context-menu click handling, which divides by its own window zoom — but that's a different coordinate space and isn't on the input path. Mentioned only to confirm the input path is genuinely untransformed.)

### Why I think this supports the navigation-triggered theory (rather than "Windows scales the buffer")

This is the part I'd most like to get a maintainer's read on. The evidence so far in this thread points at Chromium failing to (re)negotiate the renderer buffer scale for a *navigated-to* page, and I can now say the same holds with **zero** desktop-side scaling on Windows:

- If the mechanism were "Windows/DWM gives the renderer a differently-scaled buffer than the input path expects," I'd expect it to track the desktop scale — and at 100% scale it shouldn't appear at all. It does.
- That matches the `about:blank` (no mis-scale) → `example.com` (mis-scale appears) flip: the scale factor is a **per-document, post-navigation** property, and it's present on Windows too, independent of compositor/desktop scale settings.
- And because the app-level zoom (150% vs 100%) changes nothing, the scale factor in play cannot be the window's own zoom either — it's the guest page's DPR, exactly as diagnosed in this thread.

So this is now a second OS (after the original Wayland/Linux reports) where the mis-scale appears with no fractional scaling configured *anywhere*, which I'd read as pointing more firmly at the per-page buffer-scale negotiation in the renderer/input pipeline than at an OS/compositor scaling difference.

### Question for maintainers

Given the above, is there a known Chromium bug or M128+ change around renderer buffer scale vs. `sendInputEvent`'s input scale for **non-first** (navigated) pages that this is likely tracking? If so, is there a workaround on the Electron side (e.g., a `webContents`/`webview` flag or a post-`did-finish-load` call that forces the input coordinate space back to CSS pixels) that we should be calling, before assuming a host-side coordinate correction is the only available mitigation?

Happy to share the host app's input path and/or a minimal Electron repro if it's useful to isolate.

No Chromium or Electron regression here, this is a persisted zoom level rather than a DPR/input bug. Electron remembers zoom per host in the app's `Preferences` (`partition.per_host_zoom_levels`), and a `devicePixelRatio` of `1.2559...` is exactly zoom level `1.25` (`1.2 ** 1.25`). That's why `about:blank` reports `1` and `example.com` doesn't. Every `electron script.js` run shares the same default `userData`, so a zoom set on `example.com` in any earlier run sticks around (my guess is the 125% zoom testing).

`sendInputEvent` coordinates are in window DIPs, not CSS pixels, so under a page zoom they land at `x / zoomFactor`, which matches your numbers. I can reproduce your table exactly by calling `setZoomLevel(1.25)` once and then running a fresh process that never touches zoom: `(200,150)` lands at `(159,119)` and `(400,300)` at `(318,238)`. With a clean `userData` they land where they were sent.

Either reset the zoom (`webContents.setZoomLevel(0)`, or use a fresh `userData`) or convert your CSS coordinates first:

```js
const f = webContents.getZoomFactor()
webContents.sendInputEvent({ type: 'mouseDown', x: Math.round(cssX * f), y: Math.round(cssY * f), button: 'left', clickCount: 1 })
```

@gryknight9 same thing for a `<webview>`. The guest has its own zoom, so use the guest's `getZoomFactor()`, not the host app's.
I am still new to github etiquette,  but thanks for the quick response @MarshallOfSound.

nodes.title: Adapt to upstream heap profiling changes
nodes.body:
Heads-up to WG Upgrades:

Chromium is changing how heap profiling works upstream: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8258807

They’re adding it as a Perfetto data source and deleting the memlog infrastructure that Electron has been using for heap profiling so far.

When upgrading Chromium, this will probably require breaking API changes on Electron’s side:

1. Thoughts on the preferred API shape:
    - Drop the dedicated `contentTracing.enableHeapProfiling()`
    - Probably just roll it into `contentTracing.startRecording()` as described in https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51184
2. How to find the code to delete:
    - Start with https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50826
    - Delete any code added back then that is no longer necessary
3. Reference for how the integration can work:
    - Chromium's own usage of the API: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8263276
    - The CL that added the Perfetto data source: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8163651
    - [Comment](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8258807/comments/9f802612_c2ae7079) by the upstream Chromium author: "it boils down to adding `ChromiumSamplingHeapProfilerConfig` to the perfetto proto config"
